core_obligations: Start from a solid lifting diagram over the base changed data and form the composite map from the original algebra to the quotient (proof lines 9354-9361).
Check that the composite is continuous and apply formal smoothness of the original map to obtain the longer diagonal arrow (proof lines 9359-9362).
Use the universal property of the tensor product to pass from that arrow to the diagonal arrow out of the base changed algebra, which is what the definition requires (proof lines 9362-9365).
proof_roadmap: Read the diagram and form the composite (proof lines 9354-9361).
Apply the hypothesis for the long arrow (proof lines 9359-9362).
Use the universal property for the short arrow (proof lines 9362-9366).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that formal smoothness for an adic topology survives an arbitrary base change of the ground ring, and the proof is a 12-line argument that works directly with the defining lifting diagram. Given a solid diagram over the new base it composes the structure maps to obtain a diagram over the old base, applies the hypothesis to get the long dotted arrow, and then uses the universal property of the tensor product to produce the short dotted arrow required by the definition; continuity of the composite is checked at the first step. The two diagonal arrows and the identification of the base changed target are the substance, and both are displayed.
